items.description: Krea 3 图像模型现已在 ComfyUI 通过 Partner Nodes 提供，主打基于参考图的生成与编辑。模型强调更快的迭代速度和更低的单张成本，支持按上传顺序引用多张参考图、保持产品标签形状材质不变的前提下修改环境光影构图，并可将生成结果作为新输入继续编辑。  阅读原文 via AIHOT · https://aihot.news/items/ee1w5w87zh8hhwwwzqm8w65rd

items.title: Claude Opus 5.5 fast mode 结束研究预览并移除等待名单
items.description: Anthropic 宣布 Claude 平台上的 Opus 5.5 fast mode 不再处于研究预览阶段，并已移除等待名单。该模式速度最高提升 2.5 倍，定价为 $8 / $40 per million tokens；现已登陆 Microsoft Foundry（Azure 托管），Google Cloud 即将支持。Claude Code 中的 fast mode 保持不变，消耗额外 usage credits。文档见 https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/build-with-claude/fast-mode  阅读原文 via AIHOT · https://aihot.news/items/e2ssy0a7scpnel6ppyl3r9f2t

items.title: ChatGPT 为 Chrome 用户新增标签页读取与控制能力
items.description: ChatGPT 官宣面向 Chrome 用户带来升级，把 computer use 能力引入 Chrome。在聊天中，ChatGPT 可以查看用户打开的标签页并汇总信息；在工作模式下，它能控制 Chrome 标签页执行操作，如发送消息、填写表单、下载文件，还可帮助整理和分组打开的标签页。  阅读原文 via AIHOT · https://aihot.news/items/bme0mytjnlk0d2lk8hf7srzoh

items.title: Meta 如何用 AI 原生工程方式开发 Forum 应用
items.description: Meta 工程团队详解如何把 AI 智能体作为开发流程参与者来构建独立 Groups 应用 Forum，采用 human-on-the-loop 模式并以验证通过的生产级产出衡量成功。Forum 在八周内达到与 Facebook Groups 的核心功能对齐，自主压测循环在开发期发现并修复了内存问题，内存占用和缺页约减半，上线后智能体还协助根因分析用户反馈。  阅读原文 via AIHOT · https://aihot.news/items/moaux5xk1dqk4pi3tsx8sabsj

items.title: Meta 开放权重模型 Muse Spark Open 上架 OpenRouter
items.description: Meta 发布开放权重模型 Muse Spark Open，现已可在 OpenRouter 使用，定位为面向编码与智能体工作的美国最强开放权重模型。模型总参数 816B、激活 42B，支持 1M token 上下文窗口，原生多模态，OpenRouter 定价为输入 $1.25/M、输出 $4.25/M，正文提到支持图像、视频、音频和 PDF 输入。  阅读原文 via AIHOT · https://aihot.news/items/bicfbjip5iq9ccp8x7sn9yw7k

items.description: Meta 发布开源权重模型 Muse Spark Open，已在 Hugging Face 以 Muse Model License 提供。模型总参数 816B、激活 42B，上下文窗口 1M token，面向编码与智能体工作流，原生多模态（图像、音频、文档），并相比 8 月发布的 Muse Spark 增加了安全后训练。  阅读原文 via AIHOT · https://aihot.news/items/s80tw5g2v22j1se4bmqejyaq4

items.title: Meta携手苹果将8160亿参数AI模型引入Mac Studio
items.description: Meta于10月15日发布开放权重人工智能模型Muse Spark Open，并与苹果合作，针对Mac Studio优化该模型的本地运行方案。 Meta表示，该模型拥有8160亿个总参数，其中每次推理实际激活的参数约为420亿，支持长达100万Token的上下文窗口，重点面向编程、复杂推理和AI代理任务。通过两台搭载M5 Ultra芯片、各配备512GB统一内存的Mac Studio，用户可以在桌面环境中运行这一规模庞大的模型，而不必完全依赖云端AI服务。 阅读全文

items.description: IT之家 10 月 16 日消息，Microsoft（微软）当地时间昨日宣布，其已经完成了新一代 SOTA 基础模型 MAI-Base-2 的预训练工作。这一模型 在性能方面强于所有参测开源权重模型 。 MAI-Base-2 总参数规模达 2.8T，活跃参数规模 80B，在 6,000 个 NVIDIA GB200 GPU 上历经 38 天训练而成。在整个训练过程中，该模型平均浮点算力利用率为 21%、有效吞吐量为 89%。 根据微软的说法， MAI-Base-2 的预训练算力效率是 DeepSeek-V4-Pro-Base 的 4~12 倍 。 微软表示，三项举措对于 MAI-Base-2 的成功预训练尤为重要：科学规模化、模型-基础设施协同设计、数据规模化。在完善 MAI-Base-2 的同时，这家科技巨头已启动 MAI-Base-3 的准备工作。 相关阅读： 《 在 OpenAI 擅长的领域打败 OpenAI：微软称自研模型仅凭对方 1/4 算力就超越同类产品 》 参考 https://microsoft.ai/news/frontier-pre-training-at-micr

items.title: 修复“假满载”：OpenAI 优化系统 / 增加算力，减少“AI 容量上限”报错

Zach Yadegari has enjoyed an immense amount of success for someone who only recently graduated from high school. Founder of the AI-fueled calorie tracking app Cal AI, Yadegari is only 19 but his company has rocketed to viral fame over the past two years. At TechCrunch Disrupt on Thursday, Yadegari shared details of that surprising rise to prominence. Cal AI, which was founded in 2024, exploded onto the internet thanks largely to Yadegari’s strategy of deploying a small army of influencers to promote the brand. The company generated over $30 million in revenue in two years and was acquired by MyFitnessPal for an undisclosed amount of money in March. Discussing his social strategy onstage, Yadegari noted that an early sign of success came when an influencer’s post about them led to approximately a thousand new users over the course of two days. “From there, we figured out, okay, this can actually work for us, and so we started recruiting influencers as fast as we could — paying as many people as possible to start posting for us,” he said. “What we saw was that it was a clear formula. It was pretty linear, but it was extremely fast. I guess linear in the sense that every post they did would get a certain number of viewers that would convert.”

Meta has launched what it calls the “most capable” open-weight model in the United States. Dubbed Muse Spark Open, the model also has the distinction of having been designed to work with Macs. The new model, which leverages 816 billion parameters and a 1 million token context window, claims to offer superior performance to other popular open-weight models, according to evaluation results released by Meta on Thursday. Muse Spark Open is natively multimodal and built for complex coding tasks and agentic labor. It has also been designed to run locally on Apple’s computers. However, you will still need a lot of power to run the model locally, with a requirement of at least 1 terabyte of RAM, per Engadget . The model will run best via the Mac Studio that comes equipped with the M5 Ultra chip. Still, if you can muster the memory, Muse Spark Open may prove a significant work horse for coding and other desktop tasks. Meta says that it paired the model with Muse Code, its AI coding terminal, and deployed it to various agentic workflows, including coding fixes for a Mastodon client that included “bug fixes, new features, [and] full build.”

Alongside the launch of the company’s new AI wearables from Bee , Panos Panay, who serves as Amazon’s SVP of Devices, Alexa & Leo, took the stage at TechCrunch Disrupt on Thursday to talk more in depth about where he sees personal computing headed. “A lot of times, what you’re doing right now — what we all do right now — is we have to remember what we’re asking our tool to do for us,” Panay began, explaining that this is how we engage with our modern smartphones. “It’s like point, shoot, return,” Panay continued. “I think where we’re headed is a world [that] starts with ambient devices.” By “ambient devices,” he means those that work quietly in the background, using sensors and AI to help you figure out what needs to be done, instead of the other way around, where you’re telling the device what you need to do.

Universal Cart can collect items from multiple retailers, turning it into a central hub for browsing and keeping track of potential purchases. Google says the cart can also help shoppers stay on top of deals and availability. The tool can send notifications when a saved product’s price drops or when an out-of-stock item becomes available again. The tool is also designed to offer more tailored help during the shopping process. Google says it can take credit card perks into account when helping users choose how to pay, and also surface relevant promo codes.

items.description: Langley’s comments come amid mounting scrutiny of Flock from privacy advocates, including the ACLU, and members of the public who are concerned about the misuse of its technology.
items.author: Aisha Malik
items.content: Last day to save up to $200 to TechCrunch Founder Summit on Oct. 16. Register now. Disrupt doors open Oct. 13. Get your pass and bring someone with you at 50% off. REGISTER NOW. Flock CEO Garrett Langley said the company’s gunshot-detection microphones detect “just gunshots,” but Flock’s website paints a far broader picture of what other ambient audio also gets picked up. Speaking onstage at TechCrunch Disrupt , the co-founder of the surveillance company defended Flock’s audio-collection product called Gunshot Detection , which listens for gunshots and other ambient audio across nearby neighborhoods to provide “earlier awareness” to potential public safety events. Flock’s website says that the company’s audio systems can pinpoint gunfire instantly, while also being able to “detect street takeovers early to stop chaos before it escalates,” and “identify severe crashes in real time so help arrives faster.” It also says they can “expand awareness beyond gunfire with alerts for car crashes, fireworks, and sideshows.” The company’s Gunshot Detection feature, announced last year, faced immediate pushback. In announcing the feature, Flock said the technology would listen out for sounds of “screaming.” Privacy groups condemned the company for listening for human voices, prompting the company to amend its website to instead say “sounds of human distress.” Flock later said it pulled the ability to detect “distress” altogether from its customers who tried it.

YouTube Music announced Wednesday the rollout of a new labeling system aimed at improving transparency around songs created with the help of generative AI. Now listeners will be able to easily identify tracks created using AI, including those involved in composition and vocals. The label will appear on the player page. Clicking on this label provides additional information about the specific role of AI in the track’s creation. Notably, these labels will also extend to the main YouTube app. YouTube said it collaborated with various music partners and deployed its own detection tools to identify AI-generated music. According to its help page , partners using YouTube can declare their work’s use of generative AI through one of three designations: Fully Gen AI, Partly Gen AI, or No Gen AI.
